title: Dot's Sleepy Yawn
markdown:
The sky was painting itself with soft pink and mellow orange, like a cozy blanket over the quiet meadow. Dot the duckling, all fluffy yellow and a little bit wobbly, was getting ready for bed. She loved her soft nest, which smelled like warm hay and sunshine. She loved the sleepy song the crickets hummed outside her little home. But there was one tiny thing that made Dot feel not quite sleepy. Every night, just when she was feeling warm and snuggled, she could not find her last yawn.

“Oh dear,” she’d peep, her little beak wiggling. “Where did my last yawn hide tonight?” She’d peek under her wing, then behind her soft tail feathers. No matter how much she looked, her last yawn was nowhere to be found. And when she could not find her last yawn, she could not quite drift off to dreamland. This made Dot feel a little puzzled.

One evening, as the first shy stars began to peek, Dot waddled over to her kind friend, Maple the cow. Maple was resting by the stream, her big body peaceful and her chewing a soft, gentle sound. “Maple,” Dot whispered, “I can’t find my last yawn again. I’ve looked everywhere.”

Maple blinked her big, gentle eyes, the colour of warm toffee. “Don’t you worry your fluffy head, little Dot,” she mooed, her voice a low, comforting hum. “We’ll look together.” Maple stood up, slow and graceful, and together they ambled out into the quiet meadow. The air smelled sweet, like clover and soft earth.

“Let’s see,” Maple murmured, nudging a patch of soft, dewy grass with her nose. The grass tickled Dot’s feet. “Did it perhaps roll under here?”

Dot peered underneath. “Nope,” she chirped. “Not here. Where did my last yawn hide tonight?”

Maple then ambled towards the stream, where little water droplets sparkled on the reeds. The water made a soft, whispering sound. “Maybe it fell near the water?”

Dot dipped her beak near the edge. Her own reflection rippled back at her. “Not here either,” she sighed. A little tickle of surprise sat in her tummy. Maybe she should just go back to her nest.

Maple sat down, her large warm form making a safe shadow. She looked at Dot with quiet understanding. “Dot,” she said softly, “do you remember our bedtime song? The one we sing every single night before you snuggle down?”

Dot tilted her fluffy head. “Our song? Oh yes, I love our song.”

Maple hummed a low, sweet melody, a tune as gentle as the evening breeze. “And how does the song end, little one? What are the very last words we sing?”

Dot thought for a moment, closing her eyes. She remembered the happy tune, the gentle words. Then, just as a little tickle started in her throat, she remembered. As Maple hummed, Dot chimed in, her voice growing a little stronger.

“Sleepy, sleepy, close your eyes so deep,” Dot sang softly.

Maple continued, her deep voice a lovely harmony. “Little duckling, time for sleep.”

Dot felt a distinct tickle in her throat. She opened her beak, a little surprised, and out came a soft, warm, perfectly lovely yawn.

“Oh,” Dot said, eyes wide. “My yawn. It was in the song all along.” A funny bubbly tickle lived in her tummy. Maple’s gentle smile made it feel all right to have been looking in the grass.

Dot and Maple walked back to Dot’s cozy nest. The moonlight shone bright and clear, making the dewdrops sparkle. Dot snuggled down into her soft feathers, wonderfully warm and safe. She closed her eyes, a gentle happy smile on her beak, and a deep, contented sigh escaped her. Soon the quiet meadow was filled only with the soft chirping of the crickets and the gentle, rhythmic breathing of a little duckling finally, truly fast asleep, dreaming happy dreams.
